newsitem.title: UK: Physical copper market in Europe thin but nervous.
newsitem.headline: Physical copper market in Europe thin but nervous.

text.p: Europe's physical copper market has been slow, with players still wary after the recent tightness on the LME and scant Chinese buying seen in the market, traders said.
"It hasn't been busy at all. We've had a couple of enquiries but nothing desperately exciting," one said.
"There is still a great deal of nervousness...Stocks are relatively low and vulnerable. Nobody wants to be short in case the tightness reappears," another trader said.
Additional buying had been hoped for now the cash/threes backwardation has narrowed to about $65 on Tuesday from $335 at the height of the tightness.
"Usually when a backwardation disappears, people who have been putting off buying come in to the market," a trader said.
But the tightness has eased gradually instead of collapsing, and buyers may have already covered themselves when prices dipped earlier.
On the consumer side, business is very much hand-to-mouth with buyers waiting in case prices fall again. "In these times management are used to low inventories," a trader said.
European semi business was particularly slow due to a sluggish construction sector, one said.
Premiums were trying to find a level now that the February date has passed and along with it the tightest dates, but they remain difficult to pinpoint in a thin market.
Chilean metal in Rotterdam was unchanged around $30/$40 a tonne over LME cash. Traders' quotes for Good Western, however, varied from $10/$20 to $30/$40 over.
L"It's quite a mixed bag, there are many different brands. I was offered some today in single figures where there was really no buying interest," a trader said.

Russian off-grade was pegged as more stable at $25/$35 a discount to LME after a wide range of plus $30 to minus $30 late last month. There's not a lot of metal around, but there's also not the pressure to sell, traders said.
Quotes for Grade A material in Britain and Italy ranged from $30 to $45 above LME, with different views to go along with the varied rates.

Looking ahead, many traders said they were waiting for buying from China, which is said to be planning to replenish its strategic reserves over the next several years. Little business, however, has been seen yet.
"The key is when and if the Chinese come in and buy. They could come in next week or in six months from now," a trader said.
